title: Fourteen Lines
text:
A sonnet is a poem with fourteen lines. Many sonnets follow a strict rhyme pattern that helps the poem feel balanced. Poets such as Shakespeare wrote sonnets about love, time, and beauty. The form asks the writer to be efficient, because every word has a clear purpose.

Some readers feel that sonnets are difficult at first. However, the rhythm of the lines often makes them easier to remember than they seem. A student who reads one sonnet each week may notice new patterns in the language. Over several months, the reader can develop a sharper ear for sound and meaning.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, how many lines does a sonnet have?
According to the second paragraph, what often makes sonnets easier to remember?
What does the first paragraph suggest about writing a sonnet?
options: The writer can use as many words as needed
The writer must choose each word with care
The writer should avoid rhyme entirely
The writer must write only about nature

questions.text: What can the reader most likely conclude from the final sentence of the passage?
options: Sonnets are only for advanced readers
Regular practice can improve a reader's skills
Sound is less important than meaning
Reading poetry quickly is the best method

vocabulary.definition: a poem with fourteen lines and a strict rhyme pattern
a match in sound between the endings of words
achieving a result without wasting words or effort
a regular pattern of stressed and unstressed sounds

paragraph_translations: Сонет — це вірш із чотирнадцяти рядків. Багато сонетів мають сувору римовану схему, яка допомагає вірші звучати гармонійно. Поети, як-от Шекспір, писали сонети про кохання, час і красу. Ця форма вимагає від автора лаконічності, адже кожне слово має чітку мету.

Деяким читачам сонети спочатку видаються складними. Проте ритм рядків часто робить їх легшими для запам'ятовування, ніж здається. Учень, який читає один сонет щотижня, може помітити нові закономірності в мові. За кілька місяців читач може розвинути гостріший слух до звуку і значення.
